title: Returning through Germany and London, and the collapse of the 1969 tour
summary: After the 1968 trip they came back via London without playing there; the follow-up bookings in 1969 collapsed along with the promoter.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: : Well after you'd finished the first European trip in 1968, Herman, you ended up in Paris, right? And you flew -- did you fly back to the United States from Paris?
No, we went back to Germany, to be
exact, and went out to England -- uh, we would always come back from London, you know, back to London.
Back from London. Oh I see, yeah. But you didn't play in London, did you?

No. No, and that's -- I really -- I'm sorry about that, because when this man gave us this other booking, and they liked the band so much in Hamburg, and they had attached to-cut so much to our booking on the next one we did, were supposed to come back over, and we -- from London we were supposed to do oh, a bunch of dates, which we hadn't never been able to do.

And I hadn't, anyway, but I heard the guys talking about it, working in London. I don't know -- how nice it was? And we never got a chance to do it. Never had the booking. Everything went bad, and we weren't able to get back over there anymore, and the man who booked us, and he went broke, and he lost his family, and I think since then he passed, and in other words, (it was) all forgotten.
But that was-- this was 1968, your first trip, we're talking about. And yet in 1969 you went back again, didn't you?
Well I mean that's the finish. The same man we went back.
Oh, you went back -- I see. '69 was where things collapsed.
